# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 1
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "besought him and implored him one by one"
- **EMET:** "we besought him and implored him one by one and entreated him"
- **LOGOS:** "We were beseeching him individually and imploring him"
- **PNEUMA:** "gathered around him one by one, pleading with him"
- **Note:** EMET retains the triple-verb piling of the Ethiopic. LOGOS consolidates to two verbs. PNEUMA replaces verbs with narrative framing ("gathered around"). Structural disagreement.

### v.2 — "lead you astray" vs. "deceives you"
- **EMET:** "lead you astray"
- **LOGOS:** "deceives you"
- **PNEUMA:** "lead you astray"
- **Note:** Minor word-choice disagreement; LOGOS alone chooses "deceives."

### v.3 — "instructions and diverse doctrines"
- **EMET:** "set up instructions and diverse doctrines"
- **LOGOS:** "establish teachings and various doctrines"
- **PNEUMA:** "construct elaborate teachings and conflicting doctrines"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "elaborate" and changes "various" to "conflicting" — interpretive addition. EMET's "instructions" is more wooden but closer to the Greek *didaskalia*.

### v.4 — "sons of perdition" vs. "children of destruction"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "sons of perdition"
- **PNEUMA:** "children of destruction"
- **Note:** Terminological disagreement. "Sons of perdition" is theologically loaded canonical phrase; PNEUMA's rendering loses the intertextual resonance.

### v.4 — Tense of divine judgment
- **EMET:** "shall God come, my Father, to raise the dead"
- **LOGOS:** "God, my Father, shall come to raise the dead"
- **PNEUMA:** "my Father will come. God himself will come"
- **Note:** PNEUMA splits the clause into two sentences and adds "himself" — expansion not in source.

### v.5 — "image of that which shall be accomplished"
- **EMET:** "image of that which shall be accomplished at the last day"
- **LOGOS:** "image of what will come to pass in the last day"
- **PNEUMA:** "image of everything that would unfold on that final day"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "everything" expands beyond the source; "unfold" is an interpretation of *teleiousthai*.

### v.6 — "angels of punishment"
- All three agree on this phrase. No disagreement.

### v.7 — Repetition of hell-tour framing
- **EMET/LOGOS:** Render the repetition of the false-prophet warning faithfully.
- **PNEUMA:** Streamlines the repetition for readability.
- **Note:** The Akhmim text repeats the deception warning; PNEUMA's compression loses the rhetorical emphasis of oral/apocalyptic style.

### v.8 — "end of the world" vs. "end of the age"
- **EMET:** "end of the world"
- **LOGOS:** "end of the world"
- **PNEUMA:** "end of the age"
- **Note:** *Aion* / *kosmos* distinction. PNEUMA's "age" is arguably more accurate for eschatological discourse; EMET/LOGOS's "world" follows traditional English convention.

### v.10 — Parable framing
- **EMET:** "As a man planted a fig tree in his garden"
- **LOGOS:** "It is like a man who planted a fig tree in his garden"
- **PNEUMA:** "Think of a man who plants a fig tree in his garden"
- **Note:** PNEUMA shifts to present tense and imperative framing ("Think of") — rhetorical addition not in source.

### v.11 — "root up" vs. "remove" vs. "tear it out by the roots"
- **EMET:** "root up this fig tree"
- **LOGOS:** "Uproot this fig tree"
- **PNEUMA:** "Dig this tree up"
- **Note:** Minor but real disagreement on the verb. PNEUMA's second reference ("tear it out by the roots") is an expansion.

### v.13 — "the first Christ whom they crucified"
- **EMET:** "the first Christ whom they crucified and thereby sinned greatly"
- **LOGOS:** "the first Christ whom they crucified and thereby sinned greatly"
- **PNEUMA:** "the true Christ, the one they crucified, committing their great sin"
- **Note:** PNEUMA changes "first" to "true" — a significant interpretive shift. The Greek/Ethiopic *protos* (first) carries eschatological meaning (first vs. second Christ); PNEUMA's "true" flattens this.

### v.14 — "he shall slay with the sword"
- **EMET:** "he shall slay with the sword"
- **LOGOS:** "he will kill with the sword"
- **PNEUMA:** "he will turn to the sword"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "turn to the sword" is idiomatic but softens the direct agency of slaying. Minor disagreement.

### v.17 — "reckoned among the good and righteous martyrs"
- **EMET:** "reckoned among the good and righteous martyrs"
- **LOGOS:** "counted among the good and righteous martyrs"
- **PNEUMA:** "counted among the faithful martyrs, the righteous ones"
- **Note:** PNEUMA changes "good" to "faithful" — a theological interpretation. "Good" (*agathos*) and "faithful" (*pistos*) are distinct terms.

---
*14 disagreements recorded. Consensus (SOPHIA) resolved: v.4 retains "sons of perdition"; v.8 uses "age"; v.13 retains "first Christ"; v.17 retains "good and righteous martyrs."*
